requirements.quote: QoS 1 Log the message to persistent storage, make it available to any interested parties, and return a PUBACK message to the sender.
requirements.condition: When processing a QoS level 1 PUBLISH message.
requirements.required_behavior: Log the message to persistent storage.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can verify that the received QoS 1 message is persisted.

requirements.quote: QoS 1 Log the message to persistent storage, make it available to any interested parties, and return a PUBACK message to the sender.
requirements.condition: When processing a QoS level 1 PUBLISH message.
requirements.required_behavior: Make the message available to interested parties.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can observe whether delivery becomes available after receipt.

requirements.quote: QoS 1 Log the message to persistent storage, make it available to any interested parties, and return a PUBACK message to the sender.
requirements.condition: When processing a QoS level 1 PUBLISH message.
requirements.required_behavior: Return a PUBACK message to the sender.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted acknowledgment type and destination are observable.

requirements.quote: QoS 2 Log the message to persistent storage, do not make it available to interested parties yet, and return a PUBREC message to the sender.
requirements.condition: When initially processing a QoS level 2 PUBLISH message.
requirements.required_behavior: Log the message to persistent storage.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can verify persistence of the received QoS 2 message.

requirements.quote: QoS 2 Log the message to persistent storage, do not make it available to interested parties yet, and return a PUBREC message to the sender.
requirements.condition: Before the later QoS 2 release step.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not make the message available to interested parties yet.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can verify that delivery is withheld during this protocol phase.

requirements.quote: QoS 2 Log the message to persistent storage, do not make it available to interested parties yet, and return a PUBREC message to the sender.
requirements.condition: When initially processing a QoS level 2 PUBLISH message.
requirements.required_behavior: Return a PUBREC message to the sender.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted response type and destination are observable.

requirements.quote: If the broker receives the message, interested parties means subscribers to the topic of the PUBLISH message.
requirements.condition: When the broker receives the PUBLISH message.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat subscribers to the PUBLISH message's topic as the interested parties.
requirements.why_checkable: Delivery targets can be compared with subscriptions for the published topic.

requirements.quote: If a subscriber receives the message, interested parties means the application on the client which has subscribed to one or more topics, and is waiting for a message from the broker.
requirements.condition: When a subscriber receives the message.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the waiting client application subscribed to one or more topics as the interested party.
requirements.why_checkable: Client-side delivery can be observed and matched to the subscribed waiting application.

requirements.quote: A PUBACK message is the response to a PUBLISH message with QoS level 1.
requirements.condition: When a PUBACK message is sent.
requirements.required_behavior: Use it as the response to a QoS level 1 PUBLISH message.
requirements.why_checkable: A protocol trace can associate each PUBACK with its triggering PUBLISH and QoS level.

requirements.quote: A PUBACK message is sent by a broker in response to a PUBLISH message from a publishing client, and by a subscriber in response to a PUBLISH message from the broker.
requirements.condition: When a broker receives a PUBLISH message from a publishing client that requires PUBACK.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the PUBACK from the broker to the publishing client.
requirements.why_checkable: The response sender, recipient, and triggering message are visible in a trace.

requirements.quote: A PUBACK message is sent by a broker in response to a PUBLISH message from a publishing client, and by a subscriber in response to a PUBLISH message from the broker.
requirements.condition: When a subscriber receives a PUBLISH message from the broker that requires PUBACK.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the PUBACK from the subscriber to the broker.
requirements.why_checkable: The response sender, recipient, and triggering message are visible in a trace.

requirements.quote: byte 1 Message Type (4) DUP flag QoS level RETAIN 0 1 0 0 x x x x
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PUBACK fixed header.
requirements.required_behavior: Set or recognize the four-bit Message Type value as 4 (0100).
requirements.why_checkable: The first fixed-header byte can be inspected bitwise.

requirements.quote: byte 2 Remaining Length (2) 0 0 0 0 0 0 1 0
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PUBACK message.
requirements.required_behavior: Set or recognize the Remaining Length value as 2.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded Remaining Length is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote: This is the length of the variable header (2 bytes). It can be a multibyte field.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the PUBACK Remaining Length field.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent a variable-header length of 2 bytes and permit the field to use multibyte encoding.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can inspect the decoded length and exercise multibyte field encoding.

requirements.quote: Contains the Message Identifier (Message ID) for the PUBLISH message that is being acknowledged.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PUBACK variable header.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Message ID of the PUBLISH message being acknowledged.
requirements.why_checkable: The PUBACK identifier can be compared with the acknowledged PUBLISH identifier.

requirements.quote: byte 1 Message ID MSB byte 2 Message ID LSB
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PUBACK variable header.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Message ID in two bytes, most-significant byte first and least-significant byte second.
requirements.why_checkable: The two variable-header bytes and their order can be inspected.

requirements.quote: Payload There is no payload.
requirements.condition: For a PUBACK message.
requirements.why_checkable: Message bytes after the two-byte variable header can be checked for absence.

requirements.quote: When the client receives the PUBACK message, it discards the original message, because it is also received (and logged) by the broker.
requirements.condition: When the client receives PUBACK for the original message.
requirements.required_behavior: Discard the original message.
requirements.why_checkable: Client state can be inspected after receipt of PUBACK.

requirements.quote: A PUBREC message is the response to a PUBLISH message with QoS level 2. It is the second message of the QoS level 2 protocol flow.
requirements.condition: During a QoS level 2 protocol flow.
requirements.required_behavior: Use PUBREC as the response to PUBLISH and as the second message in the flow.
requirements.why_checkable: A protocol trace can verify response type and ordering.

requirements.quote: A PUBREC message is sent by the broker in response to a PUBLISH message from a publishing client, or by a subscriber in response to a PUBLISH message from the broker.
requirements.condition: When a broker receives a QoS level 2 PUBLISH from a publishing client.
requirements.required_behavior: Send PUBREC from the broker to the publishing client.
requirements.why_checkable: The triggering message and response endpoints are visible in a trace.

requirements.quote: A PUBREC message is sent by the broker in response to a PUBLISH message from a publishing client, or by a subscriber in response to a PUBLISH message from the broker.
requirements.condition: When a subscriber receives a QoS level 2 PUBLISH from the broker.
requirements.required_behavior: Send PUBREC from the subscriber to the broker.
requirements.why_checkable: The triggering message and response endpoints are visible in a trace.

requirements.quote: byte 1 Message Type (5) DUP flag QoS level RETAIN 0 1 0 1 x x x x
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PUBREC fixed header.
requirements.required_behavior: Set or recognize the four-bit Message Type value as 5 (0101).
requirements.why_checkable: The first fixed-header byte can be inspected bitwise.

requirements.quote: byte 2 Remaining Length (2) 0 0 0 0 0 0 1 0
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PUBREC message.
requirements.required_behavior: Set or recognize the Remaining Length value as 2.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded Remaining Length is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote: The length of the variable header (2 bytes). It can be a multibyte field.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the PUBREC Remaining Length field.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent a variable-header length of 2 bytes and permit the field to use multibyte encoding.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can inspect the decoded length and exercise multibyte field encoding.

requirements.quote: The variable header contains the Message ID for the acknowledged PUBLISH .
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PUBREC variable header.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Message ID of the acknowledged PUBLISH message.
requirements.why_checkable: The PUBREC identifier can be compared with the acknowledged PUBLISH identifier.

requirements.quote: Payload There is no payload.
requirements.condition: For a PUBREC message.
requirements.why_checkable: Message bytes after the two-byte variable header can be checked for absence.

requirements.quote: When it receives a PUBREC message, the recipient sends a PUBREL message to the sender with the same Message ID as the PUBREC message.
requirements.condition: When a recipient receives a PUBREC message.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a PUBREL message back to the PUBREC sender.
requirements.why_checkable: A trace can verify that PUBREL follows receipt of PUBREC and is sent to its sender.

requirements.quote: When it receives a PUBREC message, the recipient sends a PUBREL message to the sender with the same Message ID as the PUBREC message.
requirements.condition: When generating PUBREL in response to PUBREC.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the same Message ID as the received PUBREC.
requirements.why_checkable: The Message IDs of the paired PUBREC and PUBREL messages can be compared.

requirements.quote: A PUBREL message is the response either from a publisher to a PUBREC message from the broker, or from the broker to a PUBREC message from a subscriber. It is the third message in the QoS 2 protocol flow.
requirements.condition: During a QoS level 2 protocol flow.
requirements.required_behavior: Use PUBREL as the response to PUBREC and as the third message in the flow.
requirements.why_checkable: A protocol trace can verify the response relationship and ordering.

requirements.quote: byte 1 Message Type (6) DUP flag QoS level RETAIN 0 1 1 0 x x x x
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PUBREL fixed header.
requirements.required_behavior: Set or recognize the four-bit Message Type value as 6 (0110).
requirements.why_checkable: The first fixed-header byte can be inspected bitwise.

requirements.quote: byte 2 Remaining Length (2) 0 0 0 0 0 0 1 0
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PUBREL message.
requirements.required_behavior: Set or recognize the Remaining Length value as 2.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded Remaining Length is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote: The length of the variable header (2 bytes). It can be a multibyte field.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the PUBREL Remaining Length field.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent a variable-header length of 2 bytes and permit the field to use multibyte encoding.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can inspect the decoded length and exercise multibyte field encoding.

requirements.quote: The variable header contains the same Message ID as the PUBREC message that is being acknowledged.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PUBREL variable header.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the same Message ID as the acknowledged PUBREC message.
requirements.why_checkable: The PUBREL and PUBREC Message IDs can be compared.

requirements.quote: Payload There is no payload.
requirements.condition: For a PUBREL message.
requirements.why_checkable: Message bytes after the two-byte variable header can be checked for absence.

requirements.quote: When the broker receives a PUBREL message from a publisher, the broker makes the original message available to interested subscribers, and sends a PUBCOMP message with the same Message ID to the publisher.
requirements.condition: When the broker receives PUBREL from a publisher.
requirements.required_behavior: Make the original message available to interested subscribers.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can verify that subscriber delivery becomes available only at this transition.

requirements.quote: When the broker receives a PUBREL message from a publisher, the broker makes the original message available to interested subscribers, and sends a PUBCOMP message with the same Message ID to the publisher.
requirements.condition: When the broker receives PUBREL from a publisher.
requirements.required_behavior: Send PUBCOMP to the publisher.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted response type and destination are observable.

requirements.quote: When the broker receives a PUBREL message from a publisher, the broker makes the original message available to interested subscribers, and sends a PUBCOMP message with the same Message ID to the publisher.
requirements.condition: When the broker sends PUBCOMP in response to PUBREL from a publisher.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the same Message ID as the received PUBREL.
requirements.why_checkable: The PUBREL and PUBCOMP Message IDs can be compared.

requirements.quote: When a subscriber receives a PUBREL message from the broker, the subscriber makes the message available to the subscribing application and sends a PUBCOMP message to the broker.
requirements.condition: When a subscriber receives PUBREL from the broker.
requirements.required_behavior: Make the message available to the subscribing application.
requirements.why_checkable: Application delivery can be observed after receipt of PUBREL.

requirements.quote: When a subscriber receives a PUBREL message from the broker, the subscriber makes the message available to the subscribing application and sends a PUBCOMP message to the broker.
requirements.condition: When a subscriber receives PUBREL from the broker.
requirements.required_behavior: Send PUBCOMP to the broker.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted response type and destination are observable.

requirements.quote: This message is either the response from the broker to a PUBREL message from a publisher, or the response from a subscriber to a PUBREL message from the broker. It is the fourth and last message in the QoS 2 protocol flow.
requirements.condition: During a QoS level 2 protocol flow.
requirements.required_behavior: Use PUBCOMP as the response to PUBREL and as the fourth and last message in the flow.
requirements.why_checkable: A protocol trace can verify the response relationship and final ordering.

requirements.quote: byte 1 Message Type (7) DUP flag QoS level RETAIN 0 1 1 1 x x x x
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PUBCOMP fixed header.
requirements.required_behavior: Set or recognize the four-bit Message Type value as 7 (0111).
requirements.why_checkable: The first fixed-header byte can be inspected bitwise.

requirements.quote: byte 2 Remaining Length (2) 0 0 0 0 0 0 1 0
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PUBCOMP message.
requirements.required_behavior: Set or recognize the Remaining Length value as 2.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded Remaining Length is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote: The length of the variable header (2 bytes). It can be a multibyte field.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the PUBCOMP Remaining Length field.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent a variable-header length of 2 bytes and permit the field to use multibyte encoding.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can inspect the decoded length and exercise multibyte field encoding.

requirements.quote: The variable header contains the same Message ID as the acknowledged PUBREL message.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PUBCOMP variable header.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the same Message ID as the acknowledged PUBREL message.
requirements.why_checkable: The PUBCOMP and PUBREL Message IDs can be compared.

requirements.quote: Payload There is no payload.
requirements.condition: For a PUBCOMP message.
requirements.why_checkable: Message bytes after the two-byte variable header can be checked for absence.

requirements.quote: When the client receives a PUBCOMP message, it discards the original message because it has been delivered, exactly once, to the broker.
requirements.condition: When the client receives PUBCOMP for the original message.
requirements.required_behavior: Discard the original message.
requirements.why_checkable: Client state can be inspected after receipt of PUBCOMP.

requirements.quote: The SUBSCRIBE message allows a client to register an interest in one or more topic names with the broker.
requirements.condition: When processing a SUBSCRIBE message.
requirements.required_behavior: Register the client's interest in one or more topic names with the broker.
requirements.why_checkable: Subscription state and the number of supplied topic names can be inspected.

requirements.quote: Messages published to these topics are delivered from the broker to the client as PUBLISH messages.
requirements.condition: When messages are published to topics registered by the client.
requirements.required_behavior: Deliver those messages from the broker to the client as PUBLISH messages.
requirements.why_checkable: Publishing to a subscribed topic can be followed by observing broker-to-client PUBLISH delivery.

requirements.quote: The SUBSCRIBE message also specifies the QoS level at which the subscriber wants to receive published messages.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a SUBSCRIBE message.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the requested QoS level for delivery of published messages.
requirements.why_checkable: The requested QoS value can be read from the subscription request.

requirements.quote: byte 1 Message Type (8) DUP flag QoS level RETAIN 1 0 0 0 0 0 1 x
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a SUBSCRIBE fixed header.
requirements.required_behavior: Set or recognize the four-bit Message Type value as 8 (1000).
requirements.why_checkable: The first fixed-header byte can be inspected bitwise.

requirements.quote: SUBSCRIBE messages use QoS level 1 to acknowledge multiple subscription requests.
requirements.condition: When sending or processing a SUBSCRIBE message.
requirements.required_behavior: Use QoS level 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The QoS bits of the SUBSCRIBE fixed header can be inspected.

requirements.quote: The corresponding SUBACK message is identified by matching the Message ID.
requirements.condition: When correlating a SUBACK with a SUBSCRIBE message.
requirements.required_behavior: Match the SUBACK and SUBSCRIBE Message IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: The Message IDs of the request and acknowledgment can be directly compared.

requirements.quote: This also handles SUBSCRIBE messages retries in the same way as PUBLISH messages.
requirements.condition: When a SUBSCRIBE message is retried.
requirements.required_behavior: Handle the retry in the same way as a PUBLISH-message retry.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's retry behavior can be compared across SUBSCRIBE and PUBLISH flows.

requirements.quote: In this example the DUP flag is set to zero (0) to indicate that the message is being sent for the first time.
requirements.condition: In the illustrated first transmission of the SUBSCRIBE message.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the DUP flag to zero to indicate first transmission.
requirements.why_checkable: The fixed-header DUP bit and transmission attempt can be inspected, but the text explicitly limits the statement to an example.
